title: Wings’ Jimmy McCulloch is arrested in Nashville | 1974
content:
Wings’ guitarist Jimmy McCulloch was arrested in the early hours of 17 July 1974.

At the time Wings were in Nashville, Tennessee, rehearsing and recording a number of songs. In the evenings the band often partied hard, and McCulloch’s heavy drinking was becoming a concern to Paul McCartney.

On 14 July, McCulloch attended a Leon Russell recording session with Wings’ drummer Geoff Britton and guitarist Denny Laine. Afterwards they were invited to party with their Nashville fixer Dixie Gamble. She was house-sitting for a friend, and brought the members of Wings and a few others.

She became alarmed, however, when McCulloch stood on an antique glass coffee table.

I thought, ‘Oh, I’ll just throw a party for ’em, and maybe that will calm things down,’ I was living in a rental apartment, so I didn’t have an appropriate space to do it, but a friend of mine had a beautiful home with a massive living room, and I was house-sitting for her. It was just Jimmy, Geoff, Denny and Alan Crowder, maybe a few others – it wasn’t a lot of people.

I felt pretty cool about it, everything was in control – until I looked up and Jimmy McCulloch was standing on my friend’s antique glass coffee table. And I thought, ‘Oh my God, I have made a serious mistake.’ I was pretty naïve about drugs; I mean, in my world, the most anybody did was smoke a little pot and have a drink – it wasn’t a heavy drug world, so I didn’t have any concept of how things get out of control quickly. I just remember having this sinking feeling because my friend had white, shag carpet in her living room, and the house was all glass. And I’m thinking, ‘Oh, my goodness, this is not good.’

Dixie Gamble, 31 May 2020
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

The party was swiftly curtailed, and the members of Wings split up to explore the Nashville nightlife. In the morning, however, McCulloch’s rented Lincoln Continental car was in the stream running through their rented farm.

The McCartneys were furious and cancelled the day’s rehearsals. The next day McCulloch and Laine turned up late, and were admonished by Paul, resulting in them walking out and another cancellation.

On the evening of 16 July, a drunk McCulloch drove a borrowed Volkswagen into the car owned by Britton’s Nashville girlfriend, Dottie. Fortunately the damage was minimal, so they all went to the Sound Shop Studio where McCartney had been recording with Chet Atkins.

McCulloch left shortly afterwards, and in the early hours of 17 July was arrested and jailed for reckless driving.

He was assigned a lawyer, William F Carpenter Jr, who arranged a night hearing at a local court. After agreeing to cover the costs for the damage to both cars, McCulloch was released. He flew back to England with Laine and Britton the following day.
